newsitem.title: FRANCE: C.banks should see to it that dollar rises - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: C.banks should see to it that dollar rises - Chirac.

text.p: The dollar is really undervalued and the U.S. Federal Reserve and other big central banks should work better together to see that it reaches a more appropriate level, French President Jacques Chirac said.
"It's absolutely clear that the dollar is truly undervalued today, which is causing our output serious harm," Chirac told Valeurs Actuelles magazine in an interview to appear on Saturday.

"There has to be better consultation between the big central banks, including the Federal Reserve, to see to it that the dollar finds a level which better reflects the competitiveness of the American economy," the magazine quoted him as saying.
An advance copy of the interview was supplied to Reuters.

Chirac also said the troubles of France's textiles industry, which is suffering because of cheaper imports from countries with weaker currencies such as Italy, proved the need for a single European currency.

And during the transition period, rules of the game should be established between those European Union countries that joined the "euro" currency club from the outset and those that were not in from the start, Chirac added.
German Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday he believed the United States had the economic potential and credibility, and also the political will, to maintain a strong dollar.
